title: Etale origin witnesses and natural unit comparison for transported functors
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-sf-categories], the comparison morphisms $
u_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}	o S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and intrinsically bounded constructible pro-etale complexes [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

Let $T,Z$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $G:D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)	o D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be a functor, and put $H=
u_Z^*G R
u_{T,*}$ on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. For any integers $r\leq s$ and $B\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ there exists $B_e\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with an isomorphism $\alpha:
u_T^*B_e\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. For every such witness, $B_e$ has cohomology in $[r,s]$ if and only if $B$ does [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. If $B$ has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], every such witness has etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], tested against every degree-zero etale module sheaf. Witness existence and cohomological interval reflection require no Tor hypothesis.

There is a natural isomorphism of derived functors $H
u_T^*\cong
u_Z^*G$ on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Write $F=
u_Z^*G$ and $\eta:\operatorname{id}	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*$ for the derived comparison unit. For each bounded constructible witness $(B_e,\alpha)$, its induced identification $\delta_{B_e,\alpha}:HB\xrightarrow{\sim}F(B_e)$ is characterized by
$$\delta_{B_e,\alpha}^{-1}=F(R
u_{T,*}\alpha)\circ F(\eta_{B_e}).$$
For $ eta:B_e	o B'_e$ and $h:B	o B'$ satisfying $h\alpha=\alpha'
u_T^* eta$, these identifications satisfy
$$\delta_{B'_e,\alpha'}\circ H(h)=F( eta)\circ\delta_{B_e,\alpha}.$$

proof.text: Put A = P.Ring and let E be the canonical exact equivalence from fixed-coefficient pro-etale module sheaves to intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves. Intrinsic finite-torsion constructibility gives finite cohomological support and constructibility of every cohomology sheaf. Bound the support by [min(a,b),b], where a and b are lower and upper bounds of that finite support. Apply the essential-image criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] to obtain a bounded constructible etale complex L and an isomorphism from its intrinsic comparison to E(B). Its cohomological bound makes L an object of D+. The exact-derived composition isomorphism identifies the intrinsic comparison with E after the fixed-coefficient comparison. Full faithfulness of the derived realization equivalence lifts the isomorphism to the fixed-coefficient categories. The compatibility isomorphism for mapDerivedCategoryPlus then gives the required alpha in D+. No Tor hypothesis occurs.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, together with Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible; bounded restriction as in the cited origin node, clause (ii).

proof.text: For an arbitrary witness alpha, compose its image under the derived intrinsic realization with mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso to identify the intrinsic comparison of B_e with E(B). Each homology functor transports vanishing along this isomorphism. Apply the interval equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Convert homologyConcentratedIn to vanishing outside [r,s] using DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff; convert constructibleInterval to the same vanishing condition by its support inclusion, retaining the original intrinsic constructibility proof hB. This proves the iff for every witness, without using any Tor hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09B1, lemma-compare-derived (2), and Tag 099V, lemma-relative-comparison (2); exact inverse image and termwise cohomology in the comparison discussion.

proof.text: Apply the reverse implication of [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] directly to A = P.Ring, the ordered interval [r,s] and the D+ object B_e. Its pro-etale premise is the intrinsic realization of the fixed-coefficient comparison of B_e. The image of alpha under derived realization identifies that object with E(B). Transport HasProEtaleTorAmplitude along this isomorphism by composing each representative isomorphism with the image of alpha; the same K-flat complex, quasi-isomorphism and all module-sheaf tensor tests then apply verbatim. This proves Tor reflection for every witness and needs no additional coefficient-prime invertibility argument.

source.place: Clause (ii), reflection for any bounded-below etale origin.

proof.text:
Write $R=R
u_{T,*}$, $N=
u_T^*$ and $F=
u_Z^*G$, so $H=FR$. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] the derived unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}RN$ is a natural isomorphism on all of $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Apply the functor $F$ to its components. This gives $\sigma_C=F(\eta_C):F(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}HN(C)$; its inverse is $F(\eta_C^{-1})$, since a functor preserves composition and identities. For $ eta:C	o C'$, unit naturality $RN( eta)\eta_C=\eta_{C'} eta$ gives $HN( eta)\sigma_C=\sigma_{C'}F( eta)$. Thus $\sigma$ is a natural isomorphism $F\cong HN$, and its inverse is the asserted $H
u_T^*\cong
u_Z^*G$. This argument uses neither bounded constructibility nor any additivity or exactness of $G$.

source.place: Tags 099V, lemma-relative-comparison (2), and 09B1, lemma-compare-derived (2); explicit functorial application of the natural comparison unit.

proof.text: For a witness $(B_e,\alpha)$ define $t_{B_e,\alpha}=H(\alpha)\sigma_{B_e}:F(B_e)\xrightarrow{\sim}HB$ and $\delta_{B_e,\alpha}=t_{B_e,\alpha}^{-1}$. Both factors are isomorphisms by Step 4 and the witness hypothesis; their explicit inverses compose in reverse order. Since $H(\alpha)=F(R(\alpha))$, this definition gives exactly $\delta_{B_e,\alpha}^{-1}=F(R\nu_{T,*}\alpha)\circ F(\eta_{B_e})$. An inverse to a fixed isomorphism is unique, so the displayed formula characterizes the identification.

source.place: Step 2 comparison prerequisites: explicit elementary description of the witness-induced identification using the unit from Step 4 of this split.

proof.text: Let $\beta:B_e\to B'_e$ and $h:B\to B'$ satisfy $h\alpha=\alpha' N(\beta)$. With the notation of Step 5, functoriality and the naturality equation proved in Step 4 give $H(h)t_{B_e,\alpha}=H(h\alpha)\sigma_{B_e}=H(\alpha')HN(\beta)\sigma_{B_e}=H(\alpha')\sigma_{B'_e}F(\beta)=t_{B'_e,\alpha'}F(\beta)$. Compose on the left with $t_{B'_e,\alpha'}^{-1}$ and on the right with $t_{B_e,\alpha}^{-1}$. Cancel each inverse pair. The result is $\delta_{B'_e,\alpha'}\circ H(h)=F(\beta)\circ\delta_{B_e,\alpha}$, as required. Neither $h$ nor $\beta$ needs to be an isomorphism.
